title: Outage avoidance release docket - weekly sync
content:
TL;DR:
Weekly release-engineering sync focused on two intersecting items: a targeted hotfix for session-eviction (HOTFIX-3412) and cadence adjustments to reduce cross-region deploy contention. We agreed on a tightened preflight checklist, a briefed fallback path, and owners for each step.

Meeting info:
Date: 2026-03-11 09:00-09:45 PT
Attendees: Marco Chen (owner), Aisha Patel, Lena Morales, Samir Gupta, Evan Li, Priya Nair (SRE on-call), Jonah Reyes (QA)
Absentees (noted): Kiran Das (out sick)

Agenda:
1) Hotfix HOTFIX-3412 status and release window options
2) Release train cadence update: deconflicting cross-region pushes
3) Change log hygiene and automated notes for customers
4) Preflight checklist gaps discovered in last canary
5) Open risks and mitigations for rollback scenarios

Discussion notes:
- HOTFIX-3412 (session-eviction edge-case): root cause narrowed to kv-cache invalidation when cache TTLs collide with autoscale-induced node churn. Reproducer added in runtime repo (see PR #1987). Severity: P2 but regresses customer long-lived streams.
- Proposed hotfix window: 2026-03-15 02:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic). Consensus: proceed if QA signoff by 03/14 23:59 UTC. Alternative: staged canary on dedicated pool if signoff slips.
- Canary thresholds tightened: error rate < 0.05% over 30m, p95 latency regression < 10%, no increase in stream disconnects > 0.01% absolute. Monitoring runbook updated (linked).
- Deployment cadence change: shift one smaller release train to start 2h later on Tuesdays to avoid overlapping with infra autoscaler maintenance windows. This reduces contention observed on 2026-03-03. Action: platform-engineering to update scheduler by 2026-03-18.
- Change log automation: agreed to append summary lines to public changelog for any hotfix with customer-visible impact. The changelog pipeline will pick up JIRA ticket title if PR contains `changelog: include` tag. Devs asked to add that tag to HOTFIX PRs.
- Preflight checklist additions (quick wins):
  * Add KV TTL distribution sanity check (script: infra/tools/kv-ttl-scan)
  * Ensure canary pool size >= 3 for cross-region tests
  * Smoke test for streaming reconnects using synthetic client (runbook step 1.2)

Decisions made:
- Approve HOTFIX-3412 deployment on 2026-03-15 window conditional on QA signoff by 03/14 23:59 UTC. (Owner: Marco Chen)
- Update release scheduler to avoid Tuesday 00:00-06:00 UTC window for small trains. (Owner: Priya Nair to coordinate with platform-engineering)
- Require `changelog: include` on all hotfix PRs that touch customer-facing paths; document enforced in PR template. (Owner: Lena Morales)

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Marco Chen: finalize backout playbook and post to runbook page (due 2026-03-12).
- Jonah Reyes (QA): complete smoke test runs against HOTFIX build and publish results (due 2026-03-14 23:00 UTC).
- Aisha Patel: create hotfix announcement draft for Trust & Safety and CS (due 2026-03-14 18:00 UTC).
- Samir Gupta: add `kv-ttl-scan` to preflight CI job and run nightly for one week (start 2026-03-12).
- Priya Nair: coordinate scheduler change with platform-engineering and confirm rollout plan (due 2026-03-18).
- Evan Li: update PR template to include changelog tag instructions + automated CI check (due 2026-03-13).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Hotfix triggers increased reconnects during rollout if node churn coincides with cache invalidation. Mitigation: staged canary on dedicated pool + conservative circuit-breaker enabled for streaming endpoints. Backout: immediate rollback to previous image and toggle `streaming-fallback` flag to `true` (runbook steps 4–6).
- Risk: Overlapping deploy and infra autoscaler can cause transient OOMs. Mitigation: delay small releases by 2h on Tuesdays; add autoscaler quiet period during deploy window for dedicated pools.
- Risk: Missing changelog entries leading to CS confusion. Mitigation: enforce PR tag and CI check that prevents merge without ticket/`changelog: include` tag for hotfix category.

Preflight checklist snapshot (new items bolded):
- All tests green (unit / integration / smoke)
- QA signoff (stamped in ticket)
- Monitoring alerts wired to on-call (pagerduty escalation tested)
- Canary gating thresholds set (see above)
- Backout playbook reviewed and verified by SRE
- **KV TTL distribution scan completed in last 24h**
- **Canary pool size >= 3 and spread across 2 regions**

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we introduce automated TTL alerts when distribution skews > 20%? (Priya to prototype)
- Long-term: consider more graceful cache draining primitives to avoid TTL collision problem; R&D spike recommended (owner: Samir).
- Evaluate whether changelog automation should include severity label for hotfixes (mechanics TBD).

Post-meeting notes / quick hits:
- HOTFIX-3412 PR (#1987) current status: ready for QA build; unit tests pass; integration flaky on internal replay tests (Jonah investigating).
- Slack thread to watch: #release-ops pin "HOTFIX-3412" (updates by Marco).
- Next meeting: 2026-03-18 09:00 PT — focus on hotfix postmortem and scheduler rollout retrospective.

Appendix: quick links
- Jira: RLX-3412 (hotfix ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987
- Runbook: internal.runbooks/redwood/release-hotfix-playbook (internal)
- Monitoring dashboard: internal.monitoring/releases/hotfix-3412-dashboard

Notes to self (informal):
- If QA slips, fallback to split-canary: 20% traffic first hour, then 50% next 2h if metrics stable. Keep CS pager on standby.
- Remember to add tidy changelog line in the PR description so it surfaces in the public release notes pipeline.
